option_relations.rationale: Unstable angina is a form of acute coronary syndrome, which can progress to myocardial infarction, but it is not equivalent to myocardial infarction itself. It represents a broader category of ischemic heart disease.

Acute non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI) is a specific type of myocardial infarction, characterized by elevated cardiac biomarkers without persistent ST-segment elevation on ECG. The Aslanger pattern refers to specific ECG findings in NSTEMI.
Coronary artery disease with acute coronary syndrome is a broader category that includes myocardial infarction. Myocardial infarction is a specific manifestation of acute coronary syndrome.

Unstable Angina due to Multi-Vessel Coronary Artery Disease is a form of acute coronary syndrome, which can progress to myocardial infarction, but it is not equivalent to myocardial infarction itself. It represents a broader category of ischemic heart disease.
